journal_lines: §a§lIron§a under the soil. §oNot a vein — too shallow, too square. Dug. Was right.
§aSomething buried here. §oThe earth over it was packed differently than the earth beside it. Investigated.
§aOld chest in the sand, lid warped by water. Still sealed well enough to keep what was inside.
§aA square shape under the grass. §oWrong shape for a root, wrong smell for stone. Dug it up.
§aWood rotted through but the lock held. Tapped it once. Opened. Contents intact.
§aThe chest had been buried in a hurry. §oThe soil pattern said so. Whoever buried it did not come back.
§aSand had sifted in around the edges but not through the lid. The lid had done its job. So had I.
§aTook what had survived the water and the years. Left the box. It had already done more than its share.
